rv.q: Along the way, the play unearths past romantic entanglements and jealousies that are ultimately less interesting than the central dilemma.
Lucy Kirkwood’s gripping, darkly funny drama is directed by Artistic Director Rachel O’Riordan, starring the Olivier Award-nominated Meera Syal.
Top-notch revival of a modern classic.
The Children leaves a scorching print on its audience.
This intriguing and thoughtful production is highly relevant in the turbulent and uncertain world in which we live.
The play’s shortcomings are still laid bare in this new production, but it’s an exciting chance to see a modern gem, that still has pertinent things to say a decade on from its premiere.
Rachel O'Riordan directs, and has created a definitive production of this important play.

The Children is thought-provoking, but the pace limits some of the character development, leaving me with more unanswered questions than answers, which at times distracts from the bigger message at the heart of this play.
I find myself thinking that his lapse was an entirely reasonable response to a drama that loops around in a vaguely mind-numbing fashion without ever reaching a satisfying crescendo.
The writing is funny, nonjudgmental and moving in how it brings radioactive threat into a Suffolk living room.

cn.t: Kirkwood's timely post-apocalyptic drama about aging nuclear scientists confronting generational responsibility earns solid praise for its thought-provoking themes and strong performances, particularly Syal's, though some find the allegory heavy-handed.
